claims.text: Controlled Al additions promote formation of discrete Al-rich eutectic barrier layers at phase interfaces in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Al-rich eutectic barrier layers inhibit interfacial coarsening.
Al-rich eutectic barrier layers inhibit phase transformations during thermal exposure.
Al-rich eutectic barrier layers inhibit phase transformations during radiation exposure.
Suppressing coarsening and phase transformation enables retention of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
The proposed initial alloy state has a homogeneous microstructure before significant Al-driven segregation.
Changing Al content and thermal processing can selectively promote or suppress Al-rich eutectic barrier-layer formation.
The relevant structural mediator is the presence of discrete Al-rich layers at grain or phase boundaries.
The Al-rich layers arrest interdiffusion by acting as diffusion barriers.
Arrested interdiffusion limits coarsening and maintains phase stability during thermal cycling and radiation exposure.
Alloys with engineered Al-rich barrier layers will coarsen less than the baseline alloy.
Alloys with engineered Al-rich barrier layers will exhibit less phase instability than the baseline alloy.
Alloys with engineered Al-rich barrier layers will retain mechanical and environmental properties better than the baseline across thermal, radiation, high-temperature, and cryogenic tests.
A critical Al-concentration and processing window permits eutectic barrier-layer formation without introducing excessive brittle phases.
Outside the proposed Al-concentration and processing window, the stabilizing effects may not occur.
